hook: Reading the same paragraph three times and retaining nothing
topic: Glymphatic waste accumulation and its effect on cognitive processing
body:
**You read the same paragraph three times. You can describe the words. You cannot tell anyone what they mean. That is not a focus problem. That is a waste problem.**

Your brain produces metabolic byproducts while you're awake — toxic proteins and cellular debris that accumulate in the spaces between neurons. The brain has a dedicated system for clearing this waste. It's called the glymphatic system, and it operates almost exclusively during deep sleep.

When deep sleep is fragmented, shortened, or suppressed — which happens with late-night screens, alcohol, inconsistent sleep timing — that clearance is incomplete. You wake up with yesterday's cognitive waste still sitting in your neural tissue.

The result is exactly what you described. Words that won't assemble. Information that passes through without sticking. A reading comprehension that feels like it belongs to a different person.

You don't have a focus problem. You have an accumulation problem. And the solution is upstream of tomorrow morning — it starts tonight.

More on that. Link in bio.
